rationale: Consolidating two accounts so each question's current statement stands on all of its retained receipts. The parent configuration question now states the scan gap as a violation reproduced by two runs, with the repair path recorded as a bound in the same account rather than as a separate latest statement. The child admission question gains a reproduction citation from the same clean run that reproduced the gap.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled a restarted node does not load the committed configuration entries that lie at or below the commit index it recovers, and this is reproduced by two runs; the gap is bounded because a configuration entry arriving afterwards restores the node's configuration to the one in force. State, evidence and limits: restoreFromCommittedLogs clamps the store's commit index, applies the recovered range through processLogs (which ends with setLastApplied(index)), and the scan loop then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1, so a configuration entry at or below that index never reaches processConfigurationLogEntry. Parsed event 0 of receipt 5e1ce9aa430842d5a9325cfecbc885f6 records the no-snapshot case: staged commit index 11 equals lastApplied 11, scan start 12, the committed LogConfiguration at index 1 outside the scan and the node's configuration empty while its log records the voter; parsed event 1 records the snapshot case: snapshot at index 22 with configuration index 1, committed LogConfiguration at index 23 adding a nonvoter, staged commit index 32, scan start 33, and the post-restart configuration reduced to the snapshot's single voter. Receipt e1ee764584564a95b3e288381dfb75d9 reproduces both observations with the same values at its indices 0 and 1 in a run whose exit code is 0. Repair path: parsed event 15 of receipt 183f75213c5a4f26a951f76784b3e54f records a restarted two-peer node with an empty configuration while its log records both voters, and parsed event 16 records that after the serving leader commits AddNonvoter at index 8 the node's configuration becomes the full three-server set in force, so the gap closes on the next configuration entry or installed snapshot. Consequences that are source-derived rather than measured: runFollower refuses to campaign when the configuration is empty, quorumSize over an empty or stale voter list is wrong, and the vote handlers' membership rejection is skipped for an empty list, which the child question measured.
counterevidence: The recovered committed entries are still applied to the FSM, and any later configuration entry or installed snapshot restores the node's configuration, so a cluster with continuing membership traffic repairs the node without operator action; receipt 183f75213c5a4f26a951f76784b3e54f shows exactly that path.

Snapshot configuration is loaded correctly by restoreSnapshot, so the gap needs a committed configuration entry between the last snapshot (or index 0) and the recovered commit index; a cluster that snapshots after every configuration change may not reach the state.
No captured test asserts configuration state after a RestoreCommittedLogs restart, so the captured suite neither contradicts nor covers this path.
limitations: Applies to nodes configured with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; with the flag off, lastApplied equals the snapshot index and the scan range is unchanged.
Measured on in-memory single-node and two-peer clusters with the repository's in-memory transport and commit-tracking store; monotonic and production log stores are not measured.
The repair observation covers an arriving configuration entry while the node is still a member of the configuration in force; the installed-snapshot repair path remains source-derived.
interpretations.joint_history: Three receipts of the same harness file answer this question together: two runs state the gap itself (5e1ce9aa430842d5a9325cfecbc885f6 and e1ee764584564a95b3e288381dfb75d9, each at its own indices 0 and 1) and one run states the repair path for the restarted node (183f75213c5a4f26a951f76784b3e54f at indices 15 and 16). The gap events and the repair events come from different scenarios inside the same file, so they are cited jointly rather than as one history.

interpretations.rationale: Current account, reproduced twice: the empty configuration left by the restart removes the membership admission check from vote and pre-vote handling, so the node admits a candidate that appears in no configuration and also adopts the requester's higher term. Event 6 of each receipt records the node's live configuration as empty with one bootstrapped voter still recorded in its log, and event 7 records both a granted RequestVote and a granted RequestPreVote for a candidate absent from any configuration, with the node's term following the requester. Mechanism from source: requestVote and requestPreVote apply their membership rejection only when their own Servers list is non-empty, a leniency documented for the bootstrapping case, so an empty list accepts any candidate; quorumSize over an empty voter list is 1. The node's own election gating is not measured here and remains source-derived (runFollower refuses to campaign when no peers are known).
counterevidence: Granting a vote while the configuration is empty is intentional for a cluster being bootstrapped; the defect is that the node's own recovery leaves the configuration empty in a cluster that is not being bootstrapped.

The probe supplied a candidate whose term was higher and whose log was at least as recent as the node's, which is what makes the grant observable; older or staler candidates are still rejected by the log-recency rules.
The node's configuration is repaired by any later configuration entry, which the parent question's account measures.
limitations: Measured on in-memory single-node clusters with the repository's in-memory transport and commit-tracking store.
Only the vote and pre-vote handlers were driven; whether the node accepts AppendEntries or leadership from the non-member, and how its own candidacy is suppressed, is source-derived.
The candidate's identity was supplied by the probe rather than produced by a real node's election, so the request is a legal message rather than a real campaign.
interpretations.joint_history: Two runs of the same harness file emitted this pair: the experiment's own receipt f418b9d6ab8841faa9ab6c35ce1fcd75 at indices 6 and 7, and the later clean run e1ee764584564a95b3e288381dfb75d9 at the same indices, whose exit code is 0.
